title: Open an item in Explorer
how_to_read: Each attempt is one line and a `details` filename in this same directory. Open a detail file ONLY when this index points you at one -- the summaries are here so you do not have to. `caused_by` is what sent the stage back; `changed` is what the attempt then touched, counted by kind. Several attempts in a row that were caused by the same stage and changed no `src` is a loop, not progress.

open.issue: C1 (derived): from a FILE in the results, the person can jump to it in Explorer: missing
C2 (derived): from a FOLDER in the results, the person can jump to it in Explorer: missing
C3 (derived): 'act on it there' — the jump lands with the item selected or opened in an Explorer window: missing
C4 (derived): 'any file or folder in the results' — every results surface offers it (largest files list, folder tree, results list, and the unreadable-folders list where it names a folder): missing

odd-names-selected-exactly-in-explorer: needs first: A reveal path that does not depend on SHParseDisplayName(full path) for names ending in '.' or ' ', reserved device names such as 'con', and anything inside a folder with such a name. Un…

Does PS-007's 'jump to it in Explorer and act on it there' accept landing on the nearest addressable ancestor (with the item's name in the status line) for items whose names Explorer mis-parses: trailing '.' or ' ', reserved device names, and anything under such a folder? Or must those items be selected exactly? Exact selection needs the untested route the odd-names spike named (a child PIDL built through IShellFolder on the parent), which adds a component and changes Plan's contract.
PathOf as a switch over four row types versus a shared IHasPath interface (or one common property name) on the rows. The switch was kept because it is four types and needs no new abstraction.

Fallback landing: highlight the nearest addressable ancestor in its own parent (measured call shape, one mechanism) versus open the ancestor's contents through ShellExecute (lands where the person wants, second mechanism, unmeasured for long paths).

Gestures: context menu plus Ctrl+Enter only, with no double-click on the flat lists (largest files, top-level). Uniformity with the tree, where double-click expands, won over double-click on the lists.
Failure and fallback reporting through a single status line, rather than a dialog or a toast. Only the latest message is kept.
The two architecture rules cover the shell-API boundary and the UI-thread block. Someone may want a rule for the planner's purity, and the design judged that a testability concern, not a defect.
